title: Coca-Cola Building, Los Angeles
lede: Robert V. Derrah wrapped five industrial buildings in one ocean-liner facade for the Coca-Cola bottling plant on Central Avenue.
summary: A long white hull with rows of portholes, rivet lines, a bridge on the roof, and Coca-Cola script. Robert V. Derrah, Los Angeles, 1939.

source.label: Library of Congress: HABS CAL,19-LOSAN,31, Coca-Cola Bottling Company

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the Historic American Buildings Survey general view (HABS CAL,19-LOSAN,31-1, taken between 1972 and 1977) through its [Commons copy](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:GENERAL_VIEW_-_Coca-Cola_Bottling_Company,_1334_South_Central_Avenue,_Los_Angeles,_Los_Angeles_County,_CA_HABS_CAL,19-LOSAN,31-1.tif) at 1920 px.

styles.note: The most literal ocean-liner building of the style: a whole factory block drawn as a hull, with portholes, rivets, a bridge, and horizontal bands.

context: Robert V. Derrah designed a Streamline Moderne facade in 1939 that joined five existing industrial buildings; the building mimics an ocean liner with portholes, a catwalk, and a bridge. It is Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument No. 138, designated 5 February 1975. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola_Building_(Los_Angeles)).
observed: The block runs the full length of the street as one smooth white hull with a fully rounded corner.
Rows of round portholes of two sizes pierce the wall; some are grouped in pairs and threes.
Horizontal lines of rivets and two thin raised bands sweep along the wall and curve around the corner.
A darker band forms the base, like a waterline.
On the roof, a stepped bridge carries a flat oval sign with the Coca-Cola script.
A door with a rounded top, shaped like a ship’s hatch, sits in the wall. Script lettering “Coca-Cola Bottling Co.” is the only other sign.
interpretation: The building uses streamlining as a brand image: a factory turned into a ship suggests speed, cleanliness, and modernity. The long flat wall shows how repeated portholes and a few parallel bands carry a large surface without ornament.
borrow: Carry a long panel with only a few parallel horizontal rules and a row of circles; round one end.
Use a darker base band under a light surface, like a waterline.

images.alt: Black-and-white photograph of a long white factory building shaped like a ship's hull, with rows of round portholes, rivet lines, a rounded corner, and a bridge-like structure on the roof carrying a Coca-Cola sign.
images.caption: General view. rights.statement: HABS photographs are works of the United States government and are in the public domain; Commons marks the file public domain. The building dates from 1939, before December 1990, so it has no architectural copyright in the United States. The Coca-Cola script is a trademark that appears as part of the building.
